walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The Laffer curve was popularised in:
Solow's growth model shows long-run growth driven by:
options: Capital accumulation
Technological progress
Population growth
Government spending
Marginal cost is the total cost of producing all units.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Marginal means unimportant or small.
The change from one additional unit — marginal cost is the cost of producing one more unit; marginal utility is the satisfaction from one more unit. Marginal is incremental, not total or average.

mcqs.q: What is the technical definition of a recession?
options: A recession is when the stock market crashes.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
A recession is when prices fall and people lose jobs.
Two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth — a contraction of the economy.

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Marginal means unimportant or small.
By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
